families.source: UKHSA meningococcal disease clinical and public health management guidance
families.topic: meningococcal symptoms, laboratory confirmation, surveillance, prevention, treatment and vaccination
families.page_title: Meningococcal disease: clinical and public health management
evidence_points: UKHSA guidance supports health professionals with diagnosis, prevention and treatment of meningococcal disease.
Meningococcal meningitis or septicaemia may begin with non-specific flu-like symptoms and can progress rapidly.
Laboratory confirmation may use organism isolation from a normally sterile site or meningococcal DNA detection by PCR.
National surveillance links case investigation with vaccination programme changes and enhanced reporting.
Prevention and treatment measures include vaccination, prompt medical action and appropriate antibiotic treatment.
Suspected meningococcal disease requires urgent clinical assessment because severe illness can develop within hours.
The guidance links routine MenB, Hib/MenC and MenACWY immunisation to age-specific protection.
Travel guidance notes quadrivalent meningococcal vaccination requirements for Hajj and Umrah pilgrims.
Symptoms can occur in different orders and absence of a listed symptom does not exclude meningococcal disease.
A final classification requires current clinical, laboratory and public-health evidence rather than a symptom checklist alone.

families.source: UKHSA meningitis and septicaemia prevention and management guidance for higher education institutions
families.topic: meningococcal awareness, vaccination, preparedness and communication in higher education
families.page_title: Meningitis and septicaemia: prevention and management in higher education institutions
evidence_points: The guidance addresses prevention and management of meningococcal disease in higher education institutions.
It explains why new university entrants and freshers can face increased meningococcal risk.
It recommends raising awareness of meningitis and septicaemia signs and symptoms.
It supports encouraging first-time university entrants up to age 25 to receive MenACWY vaccination.
Institutions should plan ahead for a possible case or cluster of meningococcal disease.
The publication identifies resources that support immunisation awareness activities.
It includes best-practice communication considerations for a suspected meningococcal case.
The page is owned and managed by UKHSA and was rebranded without changing its substantive scope in July 2025.
Institutional preparedness guidance does not establish an individual clinical diagnosis or exposure status.
Case or cluster action still requires current UKHSA health-protection advice and setting-specific risk assessment.

families.source: UKHSA guidance for managing pneumococcal disease clusters in closed settings
families.topic: investigation and public health management of serious pneumococcal disease clusters
families.page_title: Managing clusters of pneumococcal disease in closed settings
evidence_points: The publication provides guidance for serious pneumococcal disease clusters in closed settings.
Covered settings include hospitals, care homes, prisons, children's day-care centres and military settings.
The guidance supports investigation as well as public-health management of clusters.
The current publication replaced interim guidance after pneumococcal conjugate vaccine programme changes.
Closed-setting assessment should consider epidemiological links between serious cases.
Management requires coordinated action proportionate to the affected setting and population.
Vaccination history and current pneumococcal programme context are relevant to cluster management.
The page identifies the guidance as a framework for public-health response rather than a standalone diagnostic tool.
A single pneumococcal case does not by itself prove that a closed-setting cluster exists.
Cluster classification and interventions require case linkage, microbiological evidence and current health-protection assessment.

families.source: UKHSA investigation guidance for Legionnaires' disease cases, clusters and outbreaks
families.topic: roles, source investigation and control for Legionnaires' disease incidents
families.page_title: Investigation of Legionnaires' disease: cases, clusters and outbreaks
evidence_points: The guidance is intended for health protection teams investigating Legionnaires' disease.
It covers single cases, clusters and outbreaks rather than only confirmed large outbreaks.
It sets out roles and responsibilities for public-health investigation and enforcement.
It highlights healthcare, travel and community settings as distinct investigation contexts.
It provides a standardised investigation framework that can be adapted to individual scenarios.
Potential exposure sources should be assessed through coordinated epidemiological and environmental investigation.
Supplementary material and background information are included in the guidance appendices.
The content is owned and managed by UKHSA, having originally been produced by Public Health England.
A suspected water source or shared location is not confirmed as the source without supporting evidence.
Control and enforcement actions must reflect the incident-specific risk assessment and applicable responsibilities.
